items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I took a little bit from Blanton, took a little bit from Israel Crosby and I put a little bit of Wilbur Ware in there

ctx.x: Right. Well, with Sonny Rollins Robbins, at that time, perhaps it was his nervousness, too, but you have to remember what you accomplished musically, which people constantly are saying. Like David Baker talks about he teaches people what you have contributed to the music. Maybe we could talk about different styles of bass playing and different peoples' contributions, because it's not clear to the average person.
Oh, yeah, well, like I said, I came out of the mold of Blanton and Israel Crosby (PROPHETIC) and a few

others -- Truck Chuck Parham (PHONETIC), John Kirby Curved (PHONETIC), oh, even Milt Hinton. Well, they all give me something, you know, with which to grow. I noticed the younger bassists, you hardly hear them mention the great bassists like Paul Chambers, you know, or Ray Brown, for that matter. Most of the young bassists don't say nothing. They hardly say anything about Oscar Pettiford. But most all the youngsters, I can tell that they followed Paul. Paul was the master. He was the master with the bow, but it…

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: some old friends of mine, a piano player, and Israel Crosby Robert Montgomery and Jimmy [Bowlin] ... playing opposite that young man

ctx.x: No drums. But Buster Bennett had a 4-piece band opposite us; they played 30 minutes and we played 30 minutes at this club -- the Lips Lower Level -- and what knocked me out, some old friends of mine, a piano player, and Israel Crosby Robert Montgomery and Jimmy [Bowlin] -- and that was another education; playing opposite that young man. I say 'young man' but playing and hearing all those beautiful notes he was putting out. With Buster and our band -- we would come close, you know, exchanging ideas.

And then somebody around the corner told Stuff Smith he needed a bass player; he was going to a club out at North Side. And so I worked for Stuff for 2 weeks. Then after Stuff, the next name I worked with was Roy Eldridge and Sonny Stitt.
